A [2, 32768] int32 tensor's last axis cycles seven negative values (-9, -5, -3, -1, -2, -4, -6), so a zero-initialized accumulator would misreport the maximum. Since 32768 is not a multiple of 7, row 1 begins one step into the cycle, putting its first-occurrence maximum at column 2 versus row 0's column 3.

A [2, 32769] uint32 tensor's last axis cycles seven values; six of seven exceed 2^31 (up to 4,294,967,290, near UINT32_MAX), so a signed comparison would misorder them. Since 32769 is not a multiple of 7, row 1 begins two steps into the cycle, moving its maximum's column from 3 (row 0) to 1 (row 1).

A rank-3 float16 tensor with 32,768-element rows exercises vec4 split-row reduction. Each component is widened before comparison, all seven cycle values are exactly representable, and ties select the first index.

A rank-3 float16 tensor with 32,769-element rows exercises scalar split-row reduction. Loaded values are widened before comparison, all cycle values are exactly representable, and ties select the first index.

select_last_index on the vec4 split-row route checks the last-index tie rule in both the segment reduction and combine. The maximum 7.0 recurs at cycle offsets 0, 2 and 5, so every segment reports a tie; the two phase-shifted rows must return 32767 and 32766.
A rank-5 middle-axis reduction exercises the rank-independent outer-axis-inner geometry.

On the split-tiled route, a 17-value cycle coprime with the 16 columns gives each column an approximately 482-way maximum tie. With select_last_index=1, each column must retain its final matching axis index across lane-local folds.
